name: Accountable Autonomy
principle: Autonomous work runs to a written goal, within bounds, and stops exactly when it should.
state_description: A run that is idle, blocked on a person, at a limit or looping is stopped, a slow run that is progressing is left alone, and every outcome is reported the same way.
hints_of_measurement: False stops and missed stops over labelled run logs; goal met within the budget on the runner that fits the job.

name: Permitted Timing
principle: Background work happens exactly when the person's settings allow and never otherwise.
state_description: A quest is worked when budget, cadence, a run-now request, a trigger and the roster all allow it, and not on any day or past any budget the person set.
hints_of_measurement: Scripted settings and clocks give the expected run or no-run decision for every combination.

name: Purposeful Work
principle: Every piece of work names the ideal or gap it serves and is judged by that intent's metric.
state_description: The AI's choice of what to do next reads like the person's own priorities, a gap under an intent is named by its exact text, and finished work leaves its solution's specification better than it found it.
hints_of_measurement: Intent-grounded pass rate; first-pass done rate on tasks that carry a slice; zero extra tokens for a person with no intents.

name: Specifications that apply are in view
principle: Every run sees the intent specifications that concern its input, and only those, at the cheapest tier that lets it decide.
state_description: The run starts from a handful of one-line specifications with their links, picked from the whole tree in the time of one model call; it reads in full only what it chose, and it is never shown a record that does not exist.
hints_of_measurement: For labelled inputs the expected specifications are in the selection, a failed model or vector call changes nothing but the cost, and the number of model calls is the number of batches.
